chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, and Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, all together from Yunus, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Regarding the height of the house, when it is raised to eight cubits, it is considered a dwelling. So when it exceeds eight, let him write at the top of the eight, the Verse of the Chair.
ai.seo_question: What is the required height for a house to be considered a dwelling in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a traditional architectural standard where eight cubits define a complete dwelling, linking spatial dimensions to spiritual protection. The requirement to inscribe Ayat al-Kursi on ceilings exceeding this height reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating divine remembrance into domestic spaces to ensure blessing and safeguarding. This practice underscores the holistic view of the home as both a physical residence and a sanctuary of faith.
